# VeoGen Architecture Documentation

## Overview

This directory contains comprehensive documentation for VeoGen's revolutionary **multi-provider AI orchestration architecture**. VeoGen doesn't compete with Google and Anthropic - we orchestrate them, becoming the intelligent conductor that routes creative tasks to the best AI for each job.

## 🧠 Core Architecture Philosophy

**VeoGen = The Conductor, Not the Orchestra**

Instead of building massive AI infrastructure, VeoGen creates a lean orchestration layer that intelligently routes tasks to the best AI providers. This creates unprecedented value while maintaining sustainable economics.

- Why "bring your own API keys" is genius
- Capital efficiency: $10M to dominate vs $300M+ to maybe compete
- Provider symbiosis instead of competition
- Technical implementation roadmap

- Text generation (Gemini 2.5, PaLM)
- Voice & speech (WaveNet, Speech-to-Text)

- Scientific & technical (AlphaFold, Quantum AI)

## 🎯 Multi-Provider Orchestration Strategy

### The Strategic Advantage Matrix

| AI Provider | Specialization | VeoGen Integration |
|-------------|----------------|-------------------|
| **🧠 Anthropic Claude** | Code generation, architecture, reasoning | Primary for app development, documentation |
| **🌐 Google AI** | Media generation, multimodal processing | Primary for video, images, music, UI design |
| **⚡ OpenAI** | Conversational AI, creative tasks | Secondary for specialized use cases |
| **🎨 Stability AI** | Alternative image generation | Fallback and cost optimization |

### Workflow Orchestration Examples

#### **📱 Complete App Generation**
```
User: "Create a meditation app"
    ↓
🧠 Claude: Analyzes requirements → Technical architecture
    ↓
🎨 Imagen: Generates UI mockups → Design system
    ↓
🎵 Lyria: Creates nature sounds → Audio assets
    ↓
💻 Claude: Implements React Native → Complete codebase
    ↓
📚 Claude: Writes documentation → User guides & API docs
    ↓
🎬 Veo: Creates promotional video → Marketing assets
    ↓
🚀 Automated: Builds, tests, deploys → App store ready
```

#### **📚 Interactive Content Creation**
```
Concept → Writing → Illustrations → Narration → Interactive Elements
Claude → Claude → Imagen → Google TTS → Claude (code)
```

#### **🎮 Game Development Pipeline**
```
Concept → Mechanics → Assets → Soundtrack → Marketing → Distribution
Claude → Claude → Imagen → Lyria → Veo → Automated
```

# VeoGen - AI Video Generator with Complete Monitoring Stack

**🚀 PRODUCTION READY** - VeoGen is a comprehensive AI-powered video generation platform with full observability, monitoring, and alerting capabilities built on Google's Veo AI technology. Now featuring advanced Movie Maker capabilities with frame-to-frame continuity and enterprise-grade monitoring.

## ✨ What's New in v2.0

### 🎬 Movie Maker Feature
- **AI Script Generation**: Create complete movie scripts from simple concepts
- **Frame Continuity**: Seamless transitions between scenes using FFmpeg
- **9 Visual Styles**: Anime, Pixar, Wes Anderson, Claymation, and more
- **Movie Presets**: Short Film, Commercial, Music Video, Feature, Story
- **Cost Management**: Built-in budget controls and cost estimation

### 🔧 Recent Improvements
- **✅ Fixed API Key Service**: Complete API key management system
- **✅ Enhanced UI**: Improved dropdown styling and navigation
- **✅ Settings Integration**: Easy access to API configuration
- **✅ Production Monitoring**: 4 comprehensive dashboards
- **✅ Security Hardening**: Encrypted API key storage
- **✅ User Manager Tool**: Standalone user management interface with enhanced readability

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- Docker and Docker Compose
- 8GB+ RAM recommended
- 50GB+ free disk space

### Installation
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone <your-repo-url>
cd veogen

# Start the complete stack
./setup.sh       # Linux/Mac
# or
setup.bat        # Windows
```

### Access Your Application
- **Main App**: http://localhost:4710
- **API Docs**: http://localhost:4700/docs
- **User Manager**: http://localhost:8083
- **Grafana**: http://localhost:4725 (admin/veogen123)
- **Prometheus**: http://localhost:4740
- **Alertmanager**: http://localhost:4745

## 🎯 Key Features

### 🤖 MCP Client Integration
VeoGen includes a powerful MCP (Model Control Protocol) client that automatically connects to all MCP servers configured in Claude Desktop. This enables seamless integration with a wide range of tools and services.

**Features**:
- Auto-discovers and connects to MCP servers
- Unified interface for all MCP tools
- Asynchronous operations with asyncio
- Comprehensive error handling and logging
- Automatic tool discovery and caching

**Usage Example**:
```python
from app.services.mcp import mcp_client

# Call any MCP tool
result = await mcp_client.call_tool(
    server_name="microsoft-365",
    tool_name="send_email",
    params={"to": "user@example.com", "subject": "Test", "body": "Hello!"}
)
```

**Documentation**: See [MCP Integration](./docs/architecture/mcp-integration.md) for details.


### 🎬 Video Generation
- **Text-to-Video**: Generate 1-60 second videos from text prompts
- **Multiple Styles**: Cinematic, realistic, animated, artistic
- **Custom Controls**: Duration, aspect ratio, motion intensity
- **Reference Images**: Upload images to guide generation

### 🎭 Movie Maker
- **Script Creation**: AI-powered multi-scene script generation
- **Scene Planning**: Automatic breakdown into 8-second clips
- **Continuity System**: Frame-to-frame continuity between scenes
- **Style Consistency**: Maintain visual style across all clips
- **User Control**: Review and edit scripts before production

### 🔐 User Management
- **Secure Authentication**: JWT-based user authentication
- **API Key Management**: Secure storage and management of API keys
- **User Settings**: Customizable preferences and defaults
- **Usage Tracking**: Monitor video generation usage and limits

### 👥 User Manager Tool
- **Standalone Interface**: Independent user management dashboard
- **Complete CRUD**: Create, read, update, delete user operations
- **Real-time Stats**: User counts, video statistics, API usage
- **Search & Filter**: Advanced user search and filtering capabilities
- **Export Functions**: CSV export for user data analysis
- **Status Management**: Active/inactive user status control

## 📊 Monitoring Stack Overview

VeoGen includes a complete observability stack:

### Core Application
- **Frontend**: React-based UI (Port 4710)
- **Backend**: FastAPI Python service (Port 4700)
- **Database**: PostgreSQL with monitoring
- **Cache**: Redis with metrics

### Monitoring & Observability
- **Grafana**: Dashboards and visualization (Port 4725)
- **Prometheus**: Metrics collection and alerting (Port 4740)
- **Loki**: Log aggregation and analysis (Port 3100)
- **Promtail**: Log shipping agent
- **Alertmanager**: Alert routing and notifications (Port 4745)
- **Node Exporter**: System metrics (Port 4750)
- **cAdvisor**: Container metrics (Port 4755)

## 📈 Dashboards & Analytics

### Available Dashboards
1. **System Overview** (`/d/veogen-overview`)
   - Service health status
   - System performance metrics
   - Active job counts
   - Real-time status indicators

2. **Video Analytics** (`/d/veogen-video`)
   - Video generation success rates
   - Performance by style
   - Duration analytics
   - Queue monitoring

3. **Infrastructure Monitoring** (`/d/veogen-infrastructure`)
   - CPU and memory usage
   - Container resource consumption
   - Disk space monitoring
   - Network metrics

4. **Error Analysis** (`/d/veogen-errors`)
   - Error rates by component
   - Real-time error logs
   - Error categorization
   - Debugging insights

### Key Metrics Tracked
- **Video Generation**: Success rate, duration, queue size, active jobs
- **Movie Projects**: Project completion, scene generation, style performance
- **System Health**: CPU, memory, disk usage, network I/O
- **Application Performance**: Request latency, error rates, throughput
- **FFmpeg Operations**: Processing time, failure rates, resource usage
- **API Usage**: Gemini API calls, token consumption, response times

## 🔔 Alerting

### Configured Alerts
- **Critical**: Service downtime, high failure rates
- **Warning**: Performance degradation, resource constraints
- **Info**: High usage patterns, maintenance notices

### Alert Channels
- **Email**: Critical and warning alerts
- **Slack**: Real-time notifications (configure webhook)
- **Webhook**: Custom integrations with VeoGen backend

### Alert Rules
- Service health monitoring
- Resource utilization thresholds
- Error rate monitoring
- Performance degradation detection
- Storage usage alerts

```
┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
│                 │    │                 │    │                 │
│    Frontend     │───▶│     Backend     │───▶│   Google Veo    │
│   (React)       │    │   (FastAPI)     │    │      API        │
│                 │    │                 │    │                 │
└─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
         │                       │
         │                       │
         ▼                       ▼
┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
│                 │    │                 │
│    Grafana      │    │   Prometheus    │
│  (Dashboards)   │◀───│   (Metrics)     │
│                 │    │                 │
└─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
         │                       │
         │                       │
         ▼                       ▼
┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
│                 │    │                 │
│      Loki       │    │  Alertmanager   │
│    (Logs)       │    │   (Alerts)      │
│                 │    │                 │
└─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
```

## 🔧 Configuration

### Environment Variables
Create a `.env` file with your configuration:

```bash
# Google Cloud & API Configuration
GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-project-id
GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-central1
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your-google-api-key
GEMINI_API_KEY=your-gemini-api-key

# Database Configuration
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://veogen:veogen123@postgres:5432/veogen

# Redis Configuration  
REDIS_URL=redis://:veogen123@redis:6379

# Application Settings
DEBUG=false
MAX_CONCURRENT_GENERATIONS=5
MAX_QUEUE_SIZE=50
GENERATION_TIMEOUT=3600

# Monitoring Settings
GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD=veogen123
ALERTMANAGER_WEBHOOK_TOKEN=your-webhook-token
```

### API Key Setup
1. **Access Settings**: Click your profile → Settings
2. **Configure API Keys**:
   - Google API Key (for Veo video generation)
   - Google Cloud Project ID
   - Gemini API Key (for AI text generation)
3. **Test Connection**: Verify your API keys work

### Grafana Setup
1. Access Grafana at http://localhost:4725
2. Login with `admin` / `veogen123`
3. Dashboards are automatically provisioned
4. Data sources are pre-configured

### Alert Configuration
1. Update `monitoring/alertmanager.yml` with your notification preferences
2. Configure Slack webhooks for real-time notifications
3. Set up email SMTP settings for critical alerts

## 📝 Logging

### Structured Logging
VeoGen uses structured JSON logging for better analysis:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "level": "INFO",
  "service": "video-generation",
  "message": "Video generation completed",
  "job_id": "job_123",
  "style": "cinematic",
  "duration": 45.2,
  "status": "completed"
}
```

### Log Categories
- **Application Logs**: General application events
- **Video Generation**: Video processing specific logs
- **Movie Maker**: Movie project logs
- **FFmpeg**: Video processing operation logs
- **Error Logs**: Centralized error tracking

## 🚨 Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

**Services won't start**
```bash
# Check Docker status
docker ps
docker-compose logs [service-name]

# Restart specific service
docker-compose restart [service-name]
```

**API Key Issues**
```bash
# Check API key service
docker-compose logs backend | grep api_key

# Verify API key configuration
curl -X GET http://localhost:4700/health
```

**Frontend Issues**
```bash
# Rebuild frontend
docker-compose build --no-cache frontend
docker-compose up -d frontend

# Check frontend logs
docker-compose logs frontend
```

**User Manager Issues**
```bash
# Check if User Manager is running
curl http://localhost:8083/health

# Start the User Manager Tool
python user_manager_server.py

# Check User Manager logs
python user_manager_server.py | grep -E "(ERROR|WARNING)"
```

**Monitoring Issues**
```bash
# Check monitoring stack
docker-compose ps | grep -E "(grafana|prometheus|loki)"

# Restart monitoring
docker-compose restart grafana prometheus loki
```

### Performance Optimization

**Resource Limits**
```bash
# Check resource usage
docker stats

# Scale services
docker-compose up -d --scale backend=3
```

**Database Optimization**
```bash
# Check database performance
docker-compose exec postgres psql -U veogen -d veogen -c "SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity;"
```

## 🔒 Security Features

### Implemented Security
- **API Key Encryption**: Secure hashing and encryption of API keys
- **JWT Authentication**: Secure user authentication with token management
- **Input Validation**: Comprehensive input sanitization and validation
- **Rate Limiting**: DDoS protection and resource management
- **HTTPS Support**: SSL/TLS encryption for data in transit

### Best Practices
- **Environment Variables**: Never commit API keys to version control
- **Regular Updates**: Keep dependencies and containers updated
- **Access Control**: Use strong passwords and limit admin access
- **Monitoring**: Monitor for suspicious activity and failed login attempts

## 🚀 Deployment

### Production Deployment
```bash
# Production environment
export NODE_ENV=production
export DEBUG=false

# Start with production settings
docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
```

### Cloud Deployment
- **AWS**: Use ECS or Fargate with Application Load Balancer
- **Google Cloud**: Deploy to Cloud Run or GKE
- **Azure**: Use Container Instances or AKS
- **DigitalOcean**: Deploy to App Platform

### Scaling
```bash
# Horizontal scaling
docker-compose up -d --scale backend=5 --scale frontend=3

# Load balancing
docker-compose up -d nginx
```

## 🤝 Contributing

### Development Setup
```bash
# Clone repository
git clone <your-repo-url>
cd veogen

# Install dependencies
cd frontend && npm install
cd ../backend && pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start development environment
docker-compose up -d postgres redis
npm start  # Frontend
uvicorn app.main:app --reload  # Backend
```

### Code Standards
- **Frontend**: ESLint + Prettier configuration
- **Backend**: Black + isort for Python formatting
- **Testing**: Jest for frontend, pytest for backend
- **Documentation**: JSDoc for JavaScript, docstrings for Python

# VeoGen Strategic Concepts

## Revolutionary Platform Evolution

VeoGen's transformation from video generation tool to **comprehensive AI orchestration platform** - connecting the best AI providers for their specialized strengths while maintaining lean, profitable architecture.

## Core Concepts

### 🎬 [Video Generation Workflows](../architecture/veogen-video-generation-flow.md)
The foundation: Google's Veo 3 orchestration for cinematic AI video creation

### 🎨 [Image Generation Workflows](../architecture/veogen-image-generation-flow.md) 
Visual content creation using Google's Imagen 4 for production-quality graphics

### 🎵 [Music Generation Workflows](../architecture/veogen-music-generation-flow.md)
Audio creation through Google's Lyria/MusicFX for commercial soundtracks

### 🎯 [3D Model Generation: The Model Maker Revolution](3d-model-generation-workflow.md)
**NEW**: Research-to-3D overnight using Claude + Imagen + Blender automation
- Historical recreations (Louis XV sofa example)
- Free overnight computation with Blender
- $3,500 expert work → $2.50 AI generation
- **Combined with Veo 3 "talkies" = Talking 3D characters**

### 🥽 [VR Environment Generation: Versailles in Virtual Reality](vr-environment-generation.md)
**REVOLUTIONARY**: Complete historical environments for social VR platforms
- Complete Louis XV Versailles bedroom → VRChat/Meta worlds
- $500K traditional VR development → $25 overnight generation
- Museum-quality historical accuracy through AI research
- **Democratizing virtual historical tourism and education**

### 🏗️ [VeoGen App Maker](veogen-app-maker.md)
Complete application development from natural language descriptions using Claude's programming excellence

### 🎼 [Google AI Generation Ecosystem](../architecture/google-ai-generation-ecosystem.md)
Comprehensive overview of Google's AI capabilities beyond core media generation

### ⚡ [AI Development Acceleration](../development/ai-capability-evolution.md)
**UPDATED**: The "twilight zone" phenomenon - AI having capabilities it doesn't know about
- iOS Claude export discovery case study
- Development timeline collapse: 18 months → 3 weeks
- **Veo 3 "talkies" breakthrough (June 2025) - we're early, not late**

## Strategic Framework

### The Conductor Philosophy
**"Be the conductor, not the orchestra"**

VeoGen orchestrates AI providers rather than competing with them:

```
Traditional AI Platform:         VeoGen Orchestration:
├─ $300M+ to maybe compete      ├─ $10M to dominate  
├─ GPU clusters & research      ├─ Engineering team
├─ Massive compute costs        ├─ Zero generation costs
├─ Always behind state-of-art   ├─ Always state-of-art
└─ High-risk market entry       └─ Provider symbiosis
```

### Multi-Provider Architecture

**Each AI for its Strengths**:
- **Claude/Anthropic**: Programming, complex reasoning, research
- **Google (Imagen/Veo/Lyria)**: Media generation excellence  
- **OpenAI**: General capabilities and emerging features
- **Specialized AIs**: As new capabilities emerge

### Economic Innovation: "Bring Your Own API Keys"

**User Economics**:
- Users pay providers directly (~$45/month)
- Users pay VeoGen for orchestration value ($49-149/month)
- No generation markup, transparent pricing

**VeoGen Economics**:
- Zero API costs (users bring keys)
- Pure orchestration revenue
- Sustainable scaling without compute costs
- 80-90% profit margins after development

## Market Timing Advantages

### Perfect Storm of Opportunities

**June 2025 Breakthrough**: Veo 3 "talkies" (not just better video quality)
- Natural speech with lip sync
- Character expression and emotion
- **Combined with 3D generation = Interactive talking characters**

**AI Development Acceleration**: 
- Complex platforms built in days (VeoGen proven)
- "Twilight zone" capabilities appearing faster than awareness
- Traditional competition trapped in old development mindsets

**Market Positioning**:
- Early to Veo 3 revolution (launched June 2025)
- Riding capability wave, not chasing
- First-mover advantage through AI development speed

## Competitive Landscape

### Against Traditional AI Platforms

| Traditional Approach | VeoGen Orchestration |
|---------------------|---------------------|
| **Compete with Google/Anthropic** | **Partner through API orchestration** |
| **Massive R&D investment** | **Leverage existing AI excellence** |
| **Always playing catch-up** | **Always state-of-the-art** |
| **High infrastructure costs** | **User-funded API access** |
| **Single-provider limitations** | **Best-of-breed combinations** |

### Against Manual Workflows

| Manual Creative Work | VeoGen Automation |
|---------------------|------------------|
| **3D Modeling**: $3,500, weeks | **AI Generation**: $2.50, overnight |
| **VR Environment Creation**: $500K+, 6-12 months | **VR Generation**: $25, overnight |

| **App Development**: $300K+, year | **App Maker**: $300, days |
| **Music Production**: $10K+, weeks | **Lyria Integration**: $10, hours |

## The "Unknown Knowns" Strategy

### Twilight Zone Development

**Core Insight**: AI capabilities exist before discovery or documentation

**Strategic Approach**:
1. **Aggressive Experimentation**: Try "impossible" workflows
2. **Rapid Integration**: Connect capabilities as discovered  
3. **Competitive Moats**: Undocumented capabilities = temporary advantages
4. **Continuous Discovery**: What else can current AIs already do?

**Examples Already Likely Functional**:
- Advanced 3D generation with Blender automation
- Interactive media workflows combining multiple AIs
- Complex app generation with deployment automation
- Real-time collaborative AI editing

## 🎯 Multi-Provider Orchestration Strategy

### The Strategic Advantage Matrix

| AI Provider | Best For | VeoGen Usage |
|-------------|----------|--------------|
| **🧠 Anthropic Claude** | Code, architecture, reasoning | App development, documentation, complex logic |
| **🌐 Google AI** | Media generation, multimodal | Video, images, music, UI design, real-time |
| **⚡ OpenAI** | Conversation, creativity | User interaction, alternative solutions |
| **🎨 Others** | Specialized tasks | Cost optimization, niche capabilities |

### Complete Workflow Examples

#### **📱 App Development: "Create a meditation app"**
```
1. 🧠 Claude analyzes → Technical architecture + feature specs
2. 🎨 Imagen generates → Professional UI mockups + design system
3. 🎵 Lyria creates → Custom nature sounds + meditation music
4. 💻 Claude implements → Complete React Native codebase + tests
5. 📚 Claude documents → User manual + API documentation
6. 🎬 Veo produces → Promotional video + marketing assets
7. 🏭 3D Printer creates → Physical zen stones + meditation accessories
8. 🚀 Automated → Builds, tests, deploys to app stores

Result: Production-ready app + physical products in 5 minutes
```

#### **📚 Interactive Content: "Educational course on AI"**
```
Claude (structure) → Imagen (visuals) → Lyria (audio) → Veo (videos) → Claude (interactivity)

Result: Complete course with videos, assessments, interactive elements
```

# VeoGen MCP Integration Guide

## Overview

VeoGen leverages multiple MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to create a comprehensive AI-powered creative workflow. This integration guide explains how EverArt, Blender, and other MCP tools work together to transform ideas into reality.

## Available MCP Integrations

### Core Creative Tools

1. **[EverArt MCP](everart-mcp-integration.md)**
   - AI image generation with FLUX1.1, Stable Diffusion 3.5, and Recraft
   - Reference image creation for 3D modeling
   - Concept art and visualization

2. **[Blender MCP](blender-mcp-integration.md)**
   - AI-controlled 3D modeling and animation
   - Natural language 3D creation
   - VR/AR asset generation

3. **[VRChat Integration](vrchat-content-creation.md)**
   - VR world creation and optimization
   - Social VR content deployment
   - Performance optimization for VR

4. **[Reaper DAW MCP](reaper-daw-mcp-integration.md)**
   - AI-powered music and audio generation
   - Automated mixing and mastering
   - Environmental audio design

5. **[OBS Studio MCP](obs-mcp-integration.md)**
   - Video production and streaming automation
   - Scene management and recording
   - Content creation workflows

## The Saturday Sofa Project: Complete MCP Workflow

### 9:00 AM - 10:00 AM: Research & Reference Generation

**Step 1: Historical Research**
```
User: "I want to create a Louis XV sofa for VRChat. Research the historical style and generate reference images."

AI Process:
1. Web search for Louis XV furniture characteristics
2. Analyze historical design elements
3. Generate comprehensive style guide
```

**Step 2: Reference Image Generation (EverArt MCP)**
```
Prompt: "Louis XV sofa, ornate French baroque style, gold leaf carved frame, burgundy velvet upholstery, rococo patterns, museum lighting, multiple angles, 4K resolution"

EverArt Response:
- Model: 9000:FLUX1.1-ultra
- Output: 4K reference images from multiple angles
- Time: 30 seconds per image
- Cost: ~$2.50 total
```

### 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM: 3D Modeling (Blender MCP)

**Step 3: Basic Structure Creation**
```
User: "Create the basic sofa structure based on the reference images."

Blender MCP Execution:
1. Analyze reference images
2. Generate base mesh with proper proportions
3. Create curved legs and frame elements
4. Apply basic materials
```

**Step 4: Detail Addition**
```
User: "Add the tufted upholstery pattern and carved details."

Blender MCP Process:
1. Create tufting geometry using displacement maps
2. Add carved decorative elements
3. Apply detailed materials and textures
4. Optimize for VR performance
```

**Step 5: Material and Texture Application**
```
User: "Apply realistic burgundy velvet and gold leaf materials."

Blender MCP Materials:
1. Velvet shader with appropriate roughness
2. Gold leaf material with metallic properties
3. UV mapping for optimal texture application
4. PBR material setup for VR compatibility
```

### 4:00 PM - 5:00 PM: VR Optimization

**Step 6: VRChat Preparation**
```
User: "Optimize this sofa for VRChat with proper LOD and performance."

Blender MCP VR Optimization:
1. Polygon reduction for VR performance
2. Texture optimization (1024x1024 max)
3. LOD generation for distance rendering
4. VRChat SDK compatibility check
```

### 5:00 PM - 6:00 PM: Environmental Enhancement

**Step 7: Room Context (Optional)**
```
User: "Create a simple Louis XV room around the sofa."

Combined MCP Workflow:
1. EverArt: Generate room reference images
2. Blender MCP: Create room geometry
3. Automatic asset population
4. Lighting setup for period atmosphere
```

### 6:00 PM: VRChat Testing

**Step 8: Live Testing**
```
User: "Export to VRChat and test with my Japanese friend."

Final Steps:
1. VRChat Unity SDK export
2. Upload to VRChat
3. Live testing in VR environment
4. Real-time feedback and iteration
```

## Economic Impact Analysis

### Traditional vs AI-Accelerated Workflow

**Traditional 3D Modeling Approach:**
- Time: 40-80 hours professional work
- Cost: $2,000-8,000 (professional 3D artist)
- Skills Required: Years of Blender experience
- Reference Creation: Additional $500-2,000 for photography

**AI-Accelerated MCP Workflow:**
- Time: 8-10 hours total (mostly automated)
- Cost: $10-50 (API costs only)
- Skills Required: Natural language communication
- Reference Creation: 30 seconds per image

**Savings:**
- Time Reduction: 85-95%
- Cost Reduction: 99%+
- Accessibility: From expert-only to anyone
- Quality: Maintained or improved

## Best Practices for MCP Integration

### 1. Workflow Planning
- Define clear objectives before starting
- Map out MCP server requirements
- Plan for iterative refinement

### 2. Quality Control
- Validate outputs at each stage
- Maintain style consistency across tools
- Test VR performance early and often

### 3. Cost Management
- Monitor API usage across providers
- Use appropriate quality levels for each stage
- Batch similar operations

### 4. Security Considerations
- Validate all generated code (especially Blender scripts)
- Use appropriate API key management
- Implement proper error handling

   - Industry-standard workflows

## Conclusion

The VeoGen MCP integration ecosystem transforms creative workflows by orchestrating multiple specialized AI tools. The Saturday Sofa project demonstrates how natural language commands can control professional-grade software across the entire creative pipeline.

Key benefits:
- **Accessibility**: Professional tools become available to everyone
- **Speed**: 90%+ reduction in development time
- **Cost**: 99%+ reduction in professional service costs
- **Quality**: Maintained or improved through AI consistency
- **Innovation**: Enables previously impossible creative workflows

This integration represents the future of content creation: AI-orchestrated, democratically accessible, and incredibly efficient. The combination of EverArt's image generation, Blender's 3D modeling, and VRChat's social VR creates a complete creative ecosystem that can transform ideas into shared virtual experiences in hours rather than months.

### User Manager Readme
Source: USER_MANAGER_README.md
```
# 👥 VeoGen User Manager Tool

A beautiful, standalone user management interface for the VeoGen platform with enhanced readability and complete CRUD operations.

## ✨ Features

### 🎭 Beautiful Interface
- **Modern Design**: Professional gradient backgrounds and card layouts
- **Enhanced Readability**: 16px fonts with 500 font weight for easy reading
- **Responsive Layout**: Works perfectly on desktop, tablet, and mobile
- **Status Indicators**: Visual badges for user status with improved visibility

### 🔧 Complete Functionality
- **✅ User Creation**: Create new users with proper UUID generation
- **✅ User Editing**: Update user information with validation
- **✅ Status Management**: Toggle active/inactive status with one click
- **✅ User Deletion**: Safe removal with confirmation dialogs
- **✅ Real-time Search**: Instant filtering by email, username, or name
- **✅ Data Export**: CSV export for analytics and reporting

### 🛡️ Security & Reliability
- **UUID Generation**: Proper UUID handling for PostgreSQL compatibility
- **Secure Password Hashing**: SHA-256 with salt for password security
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error management with user-friendly messages
- **Database Integration**: Direct connection to VeoGen PostgreSQL database

### 📊 Real-time Statistics
- **Total Users**: Live count of all registered users
- **Active Users**: Count of currently active users
- **Video Statistics**: Total videos generated across the platform
- **API Usage**: API key utilization metrics

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- VeoGen services must be running (PostgreSQL on port 4715)
- Python 3.8+ with required dependencies
- Modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

### Installation & Setup
```bash
# Ensure VeoGen is running
cd veogen
docker-compose up -d

# Start the User Manager Tool
python user_manager_server.py
```

### Access the Tool
- **Frontend Interface**: http://localhost:8083
- **API Documentation**: http://localhost:8083/docs
- **Health Check**: http://localhost:8083/health

## 🎯 Usage Guide

### 1. Creating Users
1. Click the **"➕ Add User"** button
2. Fill in the required information:
   - **Email**: User's email address (must be unique)
   - **Username**: Username for login (must be unique)
   - **Password**: Secure password (minimum 6 characters)
   - **Full Name**: Optional display name
   - **Status**: Active or Inactive
3. Click **"💾 Create User"** to save

### 2. Managing Existing Users
- **Edit User**: Click the ✏️ button to modify user information
- **Toggle Status**: Click ⏸️/▶️ to activate/deactivate users
- **Delete User**: Click 🗑️ to remove users (with confirmation)

### 3. Searching & Filtering
- Use the search bar to find users by email, username, or full name
- Search is real-time and case-insensitive
- Results update instantly as you type

### 4. Exporting Data
- Click **"📊 Export"** to download user data as CSV
- Export includes all user fields and statistics
- File downloads automatically to your default download folder

## 🔧 Technical Architecture

### Backend (FastAPI)
```python
# Core technologies
- FastAPI: Modern Python web framework
- PostgreSQL: Database integration with VeoGen
- UUID: Proper unique identifier generation
- Secure Hashing: SHA-256 with salt for passwords
- Async Operations: Non-blocking database operations
```

### Frontend (Modern Web)
```html
<!-- Core technologies -->
- HTML5: Semantic markup structure
- CSS3: Modern styling with gradients and animations
- Vanilla JavaScript: Efficient client-side operations
- Responsive Design: Mobile-first approach
- Enhanced Fonts: 16px for optimal readability
```

### Database Integration
```sql
-- Direct connection to VeoGen PostgreSQL
Host: localhost
Port: 4715
Database: veogen
User: veogen
Password: veogen123

-- User table structure compatibility
CREATE TABLE users (
    id VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,      -- UUID string
    email VARCHAR UNIQUE,        -- User email
    username VARCHAR UNIQUE,     -- Username
    hashed_password VARCHAR,     -- Secure hash with salt
    full_name VARCHAR,           -- Display name
    is_active BOOLEAN,           -- Status flag
    created_at TIMESTAMP,        -- Creation time
    -- Additional VeoGen fields...
);
```

## 🛡️ Security Features

### Password Security
- **Hashing Algorithm**: SHA-256 with UUID salt
- **Salt Generation**: Unique UUID salt per password
- **Storage Format**: `hash:salt` for secure separation
- **No Plain Text**: Passwords never stored in plain text

### Input Validation
- **Email Validation**: RFC-compliant email format checking
- **Username Validation**: Alphanumeric with special characters
- **Duplicate Prevention**: Database-level uniqueness constraints
- **SQL Injection Protection**: Parameterized queries

### Error Handling
- **Graceful Degradation**: Friendly error messages
- **Database Rollback**: Automatic transaction rollback on errors
- **Logging**: Comprehensive error logging for debugging
- **User Feedback**: Clear messages for duplicate emails/usernames

## 📊 API Documentation

### Core Endpoints

#### GET /api/users
Retrieve all users with statistics
```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "id": "uuid-string",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "username": "username",
      "full_name": "Full Name",
      "is_active": true,
      "created_at": "2025-07-09T10:00:00Z",
      "video_count": 5,
      "api_usage": 3,
      "last_login": "2025-07-09T09:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### POST /api/users
Create a new user with proper UUID generation
```json
{
  "email": "newuser@example.com",
  "username": "newuser",
  "password": "securepassword",
  "full_name": "New User",
  "is_active": true
}
```

#### PUT /api/users/{user_id}
Update existing user information
```json
{
  "email": "updated@example.com",
  "username": "updateduser",
  "full_name": "Updated Name",
  "is_active": false
}
```

#### DELETE /api/users/{user_id}
Delete a user (returns 204 on success)

#### PATCH /api/users/{user_id}/status
Toggle user active/inactive status

#### GET /api/stats
Retrieve platform statistics
```json
{
  "total_users": 150,
  "active_users": 142,
  "total_videos": 1247,
  "total_api_keys": 89
}
```

## 🔍 Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

#### "Database connection failed"
```bash
# Check if VeoGen PostgreSQL is running
docker-compose ps | grep postgres

# If not running, start VeoGen services
docker-compose up -d

# Wait for database to be ready
docker-compose logs postgres
```

#### "Port 8083 already in use"
```bash
# Find what's using the port
netstat -ano | findstr :8083

# Kill the process or change port in user_manager_server.py
# Look for: uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8083)
```

#### "Create user fails with UUID error"
- ✅ **Fixed in v2.0**: Proper UUID generation implemented
- Ensure you're using the latest version of `user_manager_server.py`
- Check that `import uuid` is present at the top of the file

#### "Font too small in table"
- ✅ **Fixed in v2.0**: Enhanced to 16px fonts
- Ensure you're using the latest version of `user_manager.html`
- Clear browser cache if styles don't update

### Debug Mode
```python
# Enable debug logging in user_manager_server.py
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

# Check server logs for detailed error information
python user_manager_server.py
```

## ⚡ Performance Optimization

### Database Queries
```sql
-- Optimized user retrieval with statistics
SELECT 
    u.id::text, u.email, u.username, u.full_name, 
    u.is_active, u.created_at,
    COALESCE(v.video_count, 0) as video_count,
    COALESCE(a.api_usage, 0) as api_usage,
    u.last_login
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) as video_count 
    FROM video_generations 
    GROUP BY user_id
) v ON u.id = v.user_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) as api_usage 
    FROM api_keys 
    GROUP BY user_id
) a ON u.id = a.user_id
ORDER BY u.created_at DESC;
```

### Frontend Optimization
```javascript
// Efficient search with debouncing
function filterUsers(searchTerm) {
    if (!searchTerm.trim()) {
        filteredUsers = [...users];
    } else {
        const term = searchTerm.toLowerCase();
        filteredUsers = users.filter(user => 
            user.email.toLowerCase().includes(term) ||
            user.username.toLowerCase().includes(term) ||
            (user.full_name && user.full_name.toLowerCase().includes(term))
        );
    }
    renderUsers();
    updateUserCount();
}
```

# VeoGen Monitoring Stack - Quick Start Guide

This guide will help you get the complete VeoGen monitoring stack up and running in minutes.

## 🎯 What You'll Get

After following this guide, you'll have:
- ✅ Complete VeoGen application running
- ✅ Real-time monitoring dashboards
- ✅ Automated alerting system
- ✅ Comprehensive logging
- ✅ Performance analytics
- ✅ Error tracking and debugging tools

## 🚀 5-Minute Setup

### Step 1: Prerequisites Check
```bash
# Check Docker is running
docker --version
docker-compose --version

# Ensure you have enough resources
# Minimum: 8GB RAM, 4 CPU cores, 50GB disk space
```

### Step 2: Start the Stack
```bash
# Linux/Mac
./setup.sh

# Windows
setup.bat
```

### Step 3: Verify Installation
After startup (2-3 minutes), check these URLs:

| Service | URL | Credentials |
|---------|-----|-------------|
| VeoGen App | http://localhost:3000 | - |
| API Docs | http://localhost:8000/docs | - |
| Grafana | http://localhost:3001 | admin/veogen123 |
| Prometheus | http://localhost:9090 | - |
| Alertmanager | http://localhost:9093 | - |

**Key metrics**:
- Service uptime status

**What you'll see**:

## 🔔 Alert Configuration

### Quick Alert Setup

1. **Email Alerts** (5 minutes):
   ```bash
   # Edit alertmanager config
   nano monitoring/alertmanager.yml
   
   # Update SMTP settings
   smtp_smarthost: 'your-smtp-server:587'
   smtp_from: 'alerts@yourcompany.com'
   smtp_auth_username: 'your-email@yourcompany.com'
   smtp_auth_password: 'your-password'
   
   # Update recipient email
   to: 'admin@yourcompany.com'
   
   # Restart alertmanager
   docker-compose restart alertmanager
   ```

2. **Slack Integration** (3 minutes):
   ```bash
   # Get Slack webhook URL from your Slack admin
   # Update monitoring/alertmanager.yml
   api_url: 'YOUR_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL'
   channel: '#veogen-alerts'
   
   # Restart alertmanager
   docker-compose restart alertmanager
   ```

### Pre-configured Alerts

| Alert | Condition | Severity | Action |
|-------|-----------|----------|--------|
| Service Down | Service offline > 1min | Critical | Immediate notification |
| High CPU | CPU > 85% for 5min | Warning | Email alert |
| High Memory | Memory > 90% for 5min | Warning | Email alert |
| High Error Rate | Errors > 5% for 2min | Warning | Slack notification |
| Slow Generation | Gen time > 30min | Warning | Team notification |
| Large Queue | Queue > 20 jobs | Warning | Monitoring alert |

## 📈 Metrics Collection

### Automatic Metrics
VeoGen automatically collects:

**Application Metrics**:
- HTTP request rates and latency
- Video generation success/failure rates
- Movie project completion times
- Queue sizes and processing times
- API response times and error rates

**System Metrics**:
- CPU usage per core
- Memory utilization
- Disk I/O and space usage
- Network traffic
- Container resource consumption

**Business Metrics**:
- Videos generated per hour/day
- Popular video styles
- User activity patterns
- Revenue-related metrics (if configured)

### Custom Metrics
Add custom metrics to your code:

```python
from app.middleware.metrics import track_video_generation

# Track video generation
track_video_generation(
    style="cinematic",
    status="completed", 
    duration=45.2
)
```

## 🔍 Log Analysis

### Log Categories
VeoGen organizes logs into categories:

1. **Application Logs**: `/app/logs/app.log`
   - General application events
   - User actions
   - System events

2. **Video Generation**: `/app/logs/video_generation.log`
   - Job start/completion
   - Progress updates
   - Generation errors

3. **Movie Maker**: `/app/logs/movie_maker.log`
   - Project events
   - Scene processing
   - Rendering status

4. **FFmpeg Operations**: `/app/logs/ffmpeg.log`
   - Video processing
   - Format conversions
   - Encoding details

5. **Error Logs**: `/app/logs/error.log`
   - All errors centralized
   - Stack traces
   - Debug information

### Searching Logs in Grafana

1. Go to **Explore** in Grafana
2. Select **Loki** data source
3. Use these queries:

```
# All errors in the last hour
{job="veogen-backend"} |= "ERROR"

# Video generation logs
{job="veogen-backend"} |= "video_generation"

# Specific job tracking
{job="veogen-backend"} |= "job_id=abc123"

# Performance issues
{job="veogen-backend"} |= "slow" or "timeout"
```

### Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

**Operational KPIs**:
- Service uptime: Target 99.9%
- Average response time: Target <200ms
- Error rate: Target <1%
- Queue processing time: Target <5min

**Business KPIs**:
- Videos generated per day
- Success rate by style
- User satisfaction metrics
- Resource efficiency ratios

### Performance Optimization

**Monitor these metrics**:
1. **Response Time**: Track API endpoint latency
2. **Throughput**: Requests processed per second
3. **Error Rate**: Failed requests percentage
4. **Resource Usage**: CPU, memory, disk utilization
5. **Queue Metrics**: Backlog size and processing rate

**Optimization actions**:
- Scale services based on load
- Optimize slow queries
- Implement caching strategies
- Monitor resource bottlenecks

# Check Docker resources
docker system df
docker system events

# Check logs
docker-compose logs backend
docker-compose logs grafana
```

### Issue: No Metrics in Grafana
```bash
# Check Prometheus targets
curl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets

# Verify metrics endpoint
curl http://localhost:8000/metrics

# Restart Prometheus
docker-compose restart prometheus
```

### Issue: Missing Logs
```bash
# Check Promtail status
docker-compose logs promtail

# Verify log files exist
ls -la backend/logs/

# Test Loki connection
curl http://localhost:3100/ready
```

### Issue: Alerts Not Working
```bash
# Check alertmanager config
docker-compose exec alertmanager cat /etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml

# Test alert rules
curl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/rules

# Check alert status
curl http://localhost:9093/api/v1/alerts
```

   # In docker-compose.yml

           cpus: '2.0'
           memory: 4G
   ```

2. **External Databases**:
   ```bash
   # Use managed PostgreSQL and Redis
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@external-db:5432/veogen
   REDIS_URL=redis://external-redis:6379
   ```

3. **Load Balancing**:
   - Configure nginx for load balancing
   - Use external load balancer
   - Implement health checks

# 🚀 Claude Code Installation Guide for Windows + VSCode

## 📋 **Prerequisites**

You have WSL2 with Ubuntu - perfect! Claude Code requires a Unix-like environment.

## 🛠️ **Step-by-Step Installation**

### **Step 1: Open WSL Ubuntu Terminal**

1. **Open WSL Ubuntu:**
   - Press `Windows + R`
   - Type `wsl` and press Enter
   - OR open Windows Terminal and select "Ubuntu"

### **Step 2: Install Node.js in WSL**

```bash
# Update package list
sudo apt update

# Install Node.js and npm
sudo apt install -y nodejs npm

# Verify installation
node --version
npm --version
```

### **Step 3: Install Claude Code**

```bash
# Install Claude Code globally
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# Verify installation
claude-code --version
```

### **Step 4: Set up Anthropic API Key**

```bash
# Set your API key (replace with your actual key)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-api-key-here"

# Make it permanent by adding to .bashrc
echo 'export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-api-key-here"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
```

### **Step 5: Test Claude Code**

```bash
# Test basic functionality
claude-code --help

# Create a test project
mkdir ~/test-claude-code
cd ~/test-claude-code

# Initialize a simple project
echo "console.log('Hello from Claude Code!');" > test.js

# Use Claude Code to improve the file
claude-code "Make this JavaScript file more robust with error handling"
```

---

## 🔗 **Integrating with VSCode**

### **Method 1: Use WSL Extension in VSCode**

1. **Install WSL Extension:**
   - Open VSCode
   - Install "WSL" extension by Microsoft
   - Install "Remote Development" extension pack

2. **Open WSL Project in VSCode:**
   - Press `Ctrl+Shift+P`
   - Type "WSL: New WSL Window"
   - OR click the WSL button in bottom-left corner

3. **Open Terminal in WSL:**
   - In VSCode, press `Ctrl+`` (backtick)
   - Make sure it shows "WSL: Ubuntu" in terminal

4. **Use Claude Code from VSCode Terminal:**
   ```bash
   # Navigate to your project
   cd /mnt/c/Users/sandr/your-project
   
   # Use Claude Code
   claude-code "Add TypeScript types to this JavaScript project"
   ```

### **Method 2: Create VSCode Tasks**

Create `.vscode/tasks.json` in your project:

```json
{
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "tasks": [
        {
            "label": "Claude Code: Improve File",
            "type": "shell",
            "command": "wsl",
            "args": [
                "-d", "Ubuntu",
                "bash", "-c",
                "cd '${workspaceFolder}' && claude-code 'Improve the currently selected file'"
            ],
            "group": "build",
            "presentation": {
                "echo": true,
                "reveal": "always",
                "focus": false,
                "panel": "new"
            }
        },
        {
            "label": "Claude Code: Add Tests",
            "type": "shell", 
            "command": "wsl",
            "args": [
                "-d", "Ubuntu",
                "bash", "-c",
                "cd '${workspaceFolder}' && claude-code 'Add comprehensive tests for this project'"
            ],
            "group": "test"
        }
    ]
}
```

### **Method 3: Create VSCode Shortcuts**

Add to `keybindings.json` (Ctrl+Shift+P → "Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts (JSON)"):

```json
[
    {
        "key": "ctrl+alt+c",
        "command": "workbench.action.tasks.runTask",
        "args": "Claude Code: Improve File"
    },
    {
        "key": "ctrl+alt+t", 
        "command": "workbench.action.tasks.runTask",
        "args": "Claude Code: Add Tests"
    }
]
```

# Update npm to latest version
npm install -g npm@latest

# Clear npm cache
npm cache clean --force

# Try installing with verbose logging
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code --verbose
```

```bash
# Check if API key is set
echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

# Test API connection
curl -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" https://api.anthropic.com/v1/complete
```

### **If Permission Issues:**
```bash
# Fix npm permissions
sudo chown -R $(whoami) ~/.npm
sudo chown -R $(whoami) /usr/local/lib/node_modules
```

# VeoGen MCP Servers Installation Guide

## Quick Installation for Claude

### 1. Log Viewer MCP Server

Add to your Claude MCP configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "veogen-log-viewer": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["C:/Users/sandr/AppData/Local/AnthropicClaude/app-0.11.6/veogen/tools/log-viewer-mcp/dist/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

### 2. User Manager MCP Server

Add to your Claude MCP configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "veogen-user-manager": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["C:/Users/sandr/AppData/Local/AnthropicClaude/app-0.11.6/veogen/tools/user-manager-mcp/dist/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

### 3. Combined Configuration

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "veogen-log-viewer": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["C:/Users/sandr/AppData/Local/AnthropicClaude/app-0.11.6/veogen/tools/log-viewer-mcp/dist/index.js"]
    },
    "veogen-user-manager": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["C:/Users/sandr/AppData/Local/AnthropicClaude/app-0.11.6/veogen/tools/user-manager-mcp/dist/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

```

## Prerequisites

1. VeoGen main system must be running (docker-compose up)
2. PostgreSQL database accessible on port 4715
3. Node.js installed and available in PATH
4. MCP servers built successfully (npm run build)

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues:

1. **Database Connection Failed**
   - Check VeoGen PostgreSQL is running on port 4715
   - Verify credentials (veogen/veogen123)

2. **Docker Commands Not Found**
   - Log viewer requires Docker to be accessible via command line
   - Check Docker is installed and in PATH

3. **Permission Errors**
   - Ensure Claude has permission to execute Node.js
   - Check file permissions on MCP server files

### Debug Mode:

Add this to your environment for detailed logging:
```bash
NODE_ENV=development
DEBUG=*
```

### Github Setup Guide
Source: docs\claude\GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md
```
# 🚀 GitHub Repository Setup Guide

## 📸 ImmichMCP Repository Setup

### 1. Create GitHub Repository
1. Go to https://github.com/sandraschi
2. Click "New repository"
3. Repository name: `immich-mcp`
4. Description: `🤖 AI-powered Immich photo management through natural language - MCP server for Claude and other AI assistants`
5. Make it Public ✅
6. Don't initialize with README (we have our own)
7. Click "Create repository"

### 2. Setup Local Repository
```bash
cd "C:\Users\sandr\AppData\Local\AnthropicClaude\app-0.11.6\ImmichMCP"

# Initialize git repository
git init

# Add all files
git add .

# Initial commit
git commit -m "🎉 Initial release: Complete ImmichMCP server v1.0.0

✅ Features:
- Complete TypeScript MCP server implementation
- 5 working tools: upload, albums, search, details, create
- MCP protocol compliance verified
- Production-ready with comprehensive documentation
- Claude integration ready

🛠️ Tools:
- immich_upload_photo: Upload photos with metadata
- immich_get_albums: List all albums
- immich_create_album: Create new albums  
- immich_search_photos: Advanced search with filters
- immich_get_photo: Get detailed photo information

🔗 Ready for natural language photo management through AI!"

# Add remote origin (replace with your actual repo URL)
git remote add origin https://github.com/sandraschi/immich-mcp.git

# Push to GitHub
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```

## 📚 CalibreMCP Repository Setup

### 1. Create GitHub Repository
1. Go to https://github.com/sandraschi  
2. Click "New repository"
3. Repository name: `calibre-mcp`
4. Description: `📚 AI-powered Calibre ebook library management through natural language - Dual-mode MCP server for Claude and other AI assistants`
5. Make it Public ✅
6. Don't initialize with README (we have our own)
7. Click "Create repository"

### 2. Setup Local Repository
```bash
cd "C:\Users\sandr\AppData\Local\AnthropicClaude\app-0.11.6\CalibreMCP"

# Initialize git repository
git init

# Add all files
git add .

# Initial commit
git commit -m "🎉 Initial release: Complete CalibreMCP server v1.0.0

✅ Features:
- Dual-mode TypeScript MCP server (local database + server API)
- Auto-detection between local and server modes
- MCP protocol compliance verified
- Production-ready with comprehensive documentation
- Claude integration ready

🛠️ Tools:
- calibre_search_books: Search books with multiple filters
- calibre_get_book: Get detailed book information and metadata

🏗️ Architecture:
- Local mode: Direct SQLite database access for performance
- Server mode: HTTP API for remote Calibre servers
- Auto-detection: Smart mode selection based on environment

🔗 Ready for natural language ebook library management through AI!"

# Add remote origin (replace with your actual repo URL)
git remote add origin https://github.com/sandraschi/calibre-mcp.git

# Push to GitHub
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```

### LICENSE (MIT License recommended)
Both repositories should include MIT license for open source community adoption.

## 🚀 After Repository Creation

1. **Star your own repositories** to show they're actively maintained
2. **Add repository descriptions** and topics/tags
3. **Enable GitHub Pages** if you want to showcase documentation
4. **Consider adding GitHub Actions** for automated testing/building
5. **Share on social media** to promote community adoption

## 🌟 Community Impact

These repositories will be the first open-source MCP servers for:
- **Photo Management**: Making Immich AI-accessible
- **Ebook Libraries**: Making Calibre AI-accessible

This contributes significantly to the MCP ecosystem and helps other developers integrate these powerful tools with AI assistants!
```

REACT_APP_API_URL=http://backend:8000

# LiveKit Configuration
LIVEKIT_API_KEY=devkey
LIVEKIT_API_SECRET=secret
LIVEKIT_WS_URL=ws://localhost:7880
LIVEKIT_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:7880
LIVEKIT_TURN_SERVER=turn:localhost:3478
LIVEKIT_TURN_USERNAME=veogen
LIVEKIT_TURN_CREDENTIAL=veogen123
LIVEKIT_TURN_CREDS=veogen:veogen123

# Development Server
HOST=localhost
PORT=3000
DANGEROUSLY_DISABLE_HOST_CHECK=true
FAST_REFRESH=false

# Frontend Environment Variables
REACT_APP_LIVEKIT_WS_URL=${LIVEKIT_WS_URL}
REACT_APP_LIVEKIT_API_KEY=${LIVEKIT_API_KEY}
REACT_APP_LIVEKIT_API_SECRET=${LIVEKIT_API_SECRET}

### Config
Source: .git\config
```
[core]
	repositoryformatversion = 0
	filemode = false
	bare = false
	logallrefupdates = true
	symlinks = false
	ignorecase = true
[remote "origin"]
	url = https://github.com/sandraschi/veogen.git
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
[branch "main"]
	remote = origin
	merge = refs/heads/main
	vscode-merge-base = origin/main
	vscode-merge-base = origin/main

```

### Media Roadmap 2025
Source: docs\projects\veogen\media-roadmap-2025.md
```
# VeoGen Media Roadmap – Q4 2025 Kickoff

## Objective
Track implementation of Flow ingest, Scene Describer, real-time prompt coaching, sound design upgrades, and compliance automation so Triple Initiatives milestones stay on schedule.

### Solo Dev Quick Checklist
- [ ] Work top-to-bottom: Phase A first, then B, C, etc.
- [ ] Keep a simple Kanban (To Do / Doing / Done) referencing these IDs.
- [ ] Update sprint column with actual week numbers you can commit to.
- [ ] If a row feels overkill, collapse it into your own issue tracker but keep status noted here.

## Phase A – Foundation (In Progress)
| ID | Work Item | Owner | Target Sprint | Dependencies | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Build Flow webhook ingest service (`backend/flow/ingest.py`) and persist project metadata | Platform (Mira) | Sprint 2025.46 | Flow API preview access | Use feature flag `flow.enabled` |
| A2 | Mirror Flow ingredient assets to storage vault with SynthID metadata checks | Platform (Luis) | Sprint 2025.46 | A1 | Coordinate with SRE for storage quotas |
| A3 | Implement Scene Describer client + metadata pipeline | Platform (Noor) | Sprint 2025.46 | Gemini Vision entitlement | Store captions in `metadata/captions/` |
| A4 | Surface Scene Describer output in asset viewer + Flow timeline | Frontend (Jules) | Sprint 2025.47 | A3 | Include manual override UX |

## Phase B – UI Expansion (Pending)
| ID | Work Item | Owner | Target Sprint | Dependencies | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Deliver Flow Studio tab (timeline, ingredient sidebar, approval checklist) | Frontend (Jules) | Sprint 2025.48 | A1, UX spec | Integrate feature flag |
| B2 | Launch Prompt Coach widget powered by Gemini Live | Frontend (Rhea) | Sprint 2025.49 | Realtime client, privacy doc | Provide accessibility toggles |
| B3 | Release Sound Design tab with AudioFX integration | Frontend (Ilan) | Sprint 2025.49 | AudioFX entitlement, UX spec | Fallback messaging for closed beta |

## Phase C – Compliance (Pending)
| ID | Work Item | Owner | Target Sprint | Dependencies | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Configure SynthID analytics dashboard + BigQuery export | SRE (Anika) | Sprint 2025.47 | Vertex access | Share metrics with Release Flash |
| C2 | Build nightly watermark audit job (`compliance/synthid_audit.py`) | Platform (Luis) | Sprint 2025.48 | C1 | Alert Release Eng on failures |
| C3 | Create Compliance Center UI in Release dashboard | Frontend (Rhea) | Sprint 2025.48 | C1 | CSV export for legal review |

## Phase D – Experiments (Optional Pilot)
| ID | Work Item | Owner | Target Sprint | Dependencies | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Pilot Gemini Live voice QA sessions with creative leads | Media AI (Sana) | Sprint 2025.50 | B2 | Capture feedback in Asana |
| D2 | Validate AudioFX loops in DAW MCP integration | Media AI (Theo) | Sprint 2025.50 | B3 | Ensure stems align with DAW tempo sync |

## Phase E – Workspace Automations (Backlog)
| ID | Work Item | Owner | Target Sprint | Dependencies | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | Create Docs “Brief to Flow” agent via Gemini Agent Builder | Productivity (Kai) | TBD | Flow GA | Requires Workspace admin approval |
| E2 | Ship Slides add-on for Imagen render sync | Productivity (Kai) | TBD | E1 | Display SynthID badge next to media |

## Tracking & Reporting
- Update status weekly in Release Flash standups.
- Mirror ticket IDs in Jira project `VEOMEDIA`.
- Use Grafana dashboard “Media Integrations” for telemetry (Flow ingest latency, Scene Describer throughput, SynthID audit results).

## Review Cadence
- Phase Gate reviews occur end of each sprint.
- Full roadmap review aligned with Triple Initiatives checkpoint or Flow GA announcement.*** End Patch


```
